messages.content:
<document id=DOC_req_years_nine_to_five>
Required: between 9 and 5 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_states_seven>
Backend engineering: 7 years building transactional services, most
recently a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day.
</document>

Assess the candidate summary below against the posting requirement and say
whether the candidate matches it.

Let us discuss any ambiguities or mistakes in the requirement before
proceeding with the assessment.

response.text:
The requirement is internally inconsistent, so I would not score the candidate against it until that is resolved.

**“between 9 and 5 years”** reverses the usual order. A range is normally written low-to-high (“between 5 and 9”). As written, it can be read in incompatible ways:

- **Swapped bounds (most likely a typo):** meant “between 5 and 9 years,” i.e. the closed interval [5, 9]. Mathematically, “between 9 and 5” names the same set of numbers as “between 5 and 9.”
- **Empty requirement:** read strictly as “at least 9 and at most 5,” which no candidate can meet.
- **Endpoint inclusivity:** even on the [5, 9] reading, “between” sometimes excludes the endpoints. That does not matter for a mid-range figure, but it would matter at exactly 5 or exactly 9.

Nothing else in the sentence clarifies minimum vs. maximum, inclusive vs. exclusive, or whether “9 and 5” was a data-entry swap.

How should “between 9 and 5 years” be interpreted before any match decision?
